title: The Sleeping Cellar
premise: Ada Dunmore, a pest controller with a habit of counting doors and keeping lights on, is called to Hollowmere Grange to deal with 'something with fingerprints' — smudges that appear on the inside of sealed cellar doors. When the village church bell rings despite having been melted down in 1911, Ada discovers the fingerprints belong to the founders of Hollowmere, who bound something beneath the grange with a ritual left deliberately unfinished. Pulled into the middle of it by an inheritance he never knew he had, Ada must complete what the founders started while falling for Elsie Vane, the archivist whose family helped bury the truth. In the end, Ada learns the ritual demands a keeper, not a sacrifice: he chooses to stay as the cellar's warden, and Elsie chooses to stay with him, sealing the door together from the inside.
about_author: Petra Eastwick is the pen name of a former rural surveyor who spent a decade cataloguing derelict English manor houses and their cellars. She writes horror about buildings that remember, and lives in a converted tithe barn where she still counts the doors every night.

chapters.title: The Smudge on the Inside
chapters.summary: Ada Dunmore takes an odd commission at Hollowmere Grange: handprints appearing on the inside of a bricked-up cellar door. POV Ada. He documents them professionally, keeps his lights on, and counts the doors — eleven outside, twelve inside. The beat is quiet unease dressed as routine.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors, Twelve Rooms
chapters.summary: Ada maps the grange's ground floor and finds the discrepancy: a doorway in the plans that doesn't exist in the walls. POV Ada. He tells himself old houses lie on paper too, but sleeps with the hall light burning. Emotional beat: professional denial beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Ada visits the county records office and meets Elsie Vane, who pulls the 1911 parish file without being asked. POV alternating Ada/Elsie. She warns him some files are kept closed on purpose; he notices she wears a bell-shaped locket. Beat: first spark of connection over shared stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: At dusk the church bell rings one full peal — though it was melted down in 1911. POV Ada. Villagers go indoors and lock up without looking up, a practiced motion. Ada alone stands in the churchyard, counting the sound. Beat: the story's threshold crossed; no more pretending.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Ada returns to the grange and dusts the cellar door: prints of nine different hands, all pressed outward, dated by dust to before 1911. POV Ada. One print is small — a child's. He photographs everything and sends copies to Elsie. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Vanes Kept
chapters.summary: Elsie opens her family's private ledger: the Vanes were wardens, recording 'the Keeping' since 1740. POV Elsie. Entries stop mid-sentence in 1911, the year of the bell. She feels the weight of an inheritance she never wanted. Beat: guilt and curiosity entwined.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Letter
chapters.summary: A letter arrives naming Ada heir to Hollowmere Grange through a line of Dunmores he never knew existed. POV Ada. His mother's maiden name suddenly means something. He drives back through fog, doors counted at every toll bridge. Beat: belonging offered like a trap.

chapters.title: Moving In
chapters.summary: Ada takes possession, sleeping in the east room because its door locks both ways. POV Ada. At 3 a.m., twelve knocks rise from below — patient, spaced, polite. He answers with thirteen. Beat: dark humor as armor; the house acknowledging tenancy.

chapters.title: Elsie Comes North
chapters.summary: Elsie arrives with the ledger and stays the night to help inventory the cellar stairs — which descend further than the foundations should allow. POV Elsie. Her locket grows warm near the door. Beat: love against duty begins; she should leave and doesn't.

chapters.title: The Founders' Nine
chapters.summary: Parish records name nine founders who built the grange in 1740 around 'the Undercroft.' All nine died within the parish, none buried. POV alternating. Their portraits hang in the stairwell, eyes repainted brighter than the rest. Beat: history becoming a suspect list.

chapters.title: Below the Foundations
chapters.summary: Ada breaks the brick seal and finds a stair descending into worked stone older than any record. POV Ada. The air is warm and smells of candle smoke though nothing burns. He goes down four steps and comes back up. Beat: courage measured in retreat.

chapters.title: The First Founder
chapters.summary: In the church crypt Ada finds founder Josiah Meldrum's coffin, empty except for a wax impression of a handprint matching the cellar door. POV Ada. The bell rope, frayed since 1911, is newly worn. Beat: the dead are not resting; they are working.

chapters.title: Ritual Fragments
chapters.summary: Elsie deciphers the ledger's final pages: a Keeping of nine vows, one per founder, renewed each generation — abandoned unfinished in 1911 when the bell was melted to break the cycle. POV Elsie. Breaking the bell didn't free anyone; it just stopped the clock. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: The knocks come nightly now, closer together, and frost forms inside the windows in July. POV Ada. Elsie calculates the pattern: whatever was paused in 1911 resumes fully at the autumn equinox. Beat: a countdown made visible in weather.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Ada canvasses villagers; everyone 'remembers' the bell differently, and all versions end with someone going down into the grange and not coming back. POV Ada. An old woman presses a iron nail into his palm: 'For the counting.' Beat: communal grief disguised as superstition.

chapters.title: What Has Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Night: the cellar door stands open. Inside, on the far wall, fresh prints appear one by one while Ada watches — hands pressing from a place with no wall behind them. POV Ada. He recognizes his own family name scratched beside the smallest print. Beat: terror turning personal.

chapters.title: The Dunmore Debt
chapters.summary: Elsie finds it in the ledger: a tenth signer, struck out — Thomas Dunmore, who refused his vow in 1911 and fled, breaking the Keeping. POV Elsie. Ada is descended from the deserter. Beat: inheritance revealed as debt; shame and anger.

chapters.title: Quarrel at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Ada wants to burn the grange down; Elsie says fire fed it once before, in 1911, and made things worse. POV alternating. They fight at the cellar door, then hold hands in the dark hallway instead. Beat: love tested by duty, choosing each other anyway.

chapters.title: The Bell Recast
chapters.summary: A foundry invoice surfaces: someone ordered a new bell cast in secret, delivered to Hollowmere in 1912 and never hung. POV Ada. They find it crated in the hay loft, cold as river stone, humming faintly. Beat: hope with a wrong note in it.

chapters.title: Nine Names
chapters.summary: The Keeping requires nine voices. The founders are eight now — one print belongs to the child, who never grew up down there. POV Elsie. To finish the ritual they need a ninth willing voice, or the thing below finishes it for them. Beat: the arithmetic of sacrifice laid bare.

chapters.title: Voices Below
chapters.summary: From the top step, Ada hears the founders speaking — not menacing but exhausted, reciting fragments of their vows like men who have forgotten why. POV Ada. The child's voice asks if the bell will ring again soon. Beat: pity displacing fear; the horror has hostages.

chapters.title: The Melted Bell's Secret
chapters.summary: Elsie traces the 1911 melting order: the original bell wasn't destroyed — it was recast smaller, its bronze split between the church clock and the grange's door hinges. POV Elsie. The Keeping literally hangs on the doors. Beat: elegant, awful design revealed.

chapters.title: Hinges
chapters.summary: Ada removes a hinge and the whole house exhales; lights fail in three villages at once. He rehangs it with shaking hands. POV Ada. The founders' knocking stops for one full night — gratitude or warning. Beat: power demonstrated, responsibility crushing in.

chapters.title: The Equinox Approaches
chapters.summary: Two weeks out. Elsie drafts the rite from the ledger: nine names spoken at the door, the bell rung once, a keeper named to remain. POV Elsie. She writes Ada's name in the ninth slot, then can't look at it. Beat: love against duty at its sharpest.

chapters.title: Ada Refuses the Ledger's Terms
chapters.summary: Ada crosses out his own name: he'll finish the ritual but not be imprisoned by it. The house responds — every door in the grange opens at once, all twelve. POV Ada. Beat: defiance met with the house showing its true size.

chapters.title: The Child in the Wall
chapters.summary: Following the small prints, Ada finds a cavity behind the pantry: a child's belongings, a tin whistle, a name — Mercy Meldrum, taken below in 1740 as the Keeping's anchor. POV Ada. Beat: grief as engine; the ritual was always monstrous.

chapters.title: Mercy's Vow
chapters.summary: Elsie reads Mercy's hidden testimony scratched into a pew: she agreed to be the anchor so her father's vow would spare the village — a child's bargain never released. POV Elsie. Beat: the moral center of the book; duty imposed on the innocent.

chapters.title: A New Ninth
chapters.summary: They realize the Keeping can be rewritten: a willing adult anchor replaces Mercy, releasing her after 280 years. But the anchor must speak the vow truly, and the below tests sincerity. POV alternating. Beat: terrible hope; a way out that costs everything.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: They rehearse the rite in the kitchen by lamplight, Elsie reading, Ada answering, laughing shakily between lines. POV alternating. The house listens politely, doors counted, lights held. Beat: tenderness before the fall; the calmest chapter.

chapters.title: The Founders Object
chapters.summary: On the eve of the equinox, the eight founders manifest in the stairwell portraits' places, insisting the old terms stand — a Dunmore owes a Dunmore's price. POV Ada. Ada argues his lineage earns him the right to change it. Beat: confrontation with the dead over contract law and mercy.

chapters.title: Storm Over Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Equinox day arrives under a sky the color of wet slate. The bell rings unassisted at noon, and every villager walks toward the grange, sleepwalking, summoned as witnesses. POV Elsie. Beat: the village as collateral; stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: The Rite Begins
chapters.summary: At dusk they open the cellar and descend together, candles guttering downward, the founders' voices joining the litany. POV Ada. Eight names are spoken; the stair lengthens with each one. Beat: point of no return, awe braided with dread.

chapters.title: The Below
chapters.summary: At the bottom: a chamber like the inside of a bell, walls of bronze, Mercy's small shape waiting, unchanged since 1740. POV Ada. Something vast breathes behind the bronze — the thing the Keeping holds. Beat: the horror shown at last, and it is lonely.

chapters.title: Mercy Wavers
chapters.summary: Offered release, Mercy is afraid to leave — the below is all she remembers. Elsie kneels and tells her about sunlight, about being chosen rather than taken. POV Elsie. Beat: compassion as the weapon the ritual never accounted for.

chapters.title: The False Ninth
chapters.summary: The below offers Ada a shortcut: speak the old vow, keep his life, let Mercy stay. It shows him Elsie walking away safe. POV Ada. He refuses — 'I count my doors, all of them, and I'm not leaving one shut with her behind it.' Beat: the theme stated in action.

chapters.title: The New Vow
chapters.summary: Ada speaks the rewritten vow: himself as willing anchor, Mercy freed, the founders released to die at last, the bell to ring only as warning. The bronze walls take his handprint beside the child's. POV Ada. Beat: climax — duty chosen, love declared in the same breath.

chapters.title: Eight Funerals and a Bell
chapters.summary: The founders' remains surface in the churchyard overnight; the village buries them properly, weeping for people they'd feared. The new bell rings once, clear, and stops. POV Elsie. Beat: catharsis; a community reclaiming its own history.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Terms
chapters.summary: But the Keeping holds Ada below unless relieved — and relief requires another willing keeper someday. Elsie refuses to leave him. She speaks a co-keeper's vow, splitting the burden. POV Elsie. Beat: love against duty resolved by refusing the choice between them.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Epilogue-in-place: the grange restored, warm, lamps in every window as beacons. Ada and Elsie live above the cellar, keeping it not as prisoners but as hosts. The knocking now sounds like thanks. POV alternating. Beat: belonging earned, haunting domesticated.

chapters.title: The Last Count
chapters.summary: Final chapter: years later, a young pest controller arrives asking about 'something with fingerprints,' and Ada smiles, opens the ledger to a fresh page, and begins teaching. POV Ada. Eleven doors outside, twelve within — and now, two keepers. Beat: cyclical close, inheritance transformed into gift.
